# weft

weft lets the prose of an R Markdown or Quarto document carry computed
values, and wording that depends on those values. It checks that what a
sentence says is still true of the data each time the document renders.
For a long report or a book, it also stops the commits that would break
the link between a number in the text and the analysis that produced it.

Every weft construct is markdown that knitr, Pandoc and Quarto already
accept. Nothing is compiled, and the file you edit is the file that
renders.

## An example

A Quarto document. The front matter turns weft on for this one document.

```` markdown
---
title: "Creek monitoring"
engine: knitr
knitr:
  opts_knit:
    weft: !expr weft::weft_setup()
---

```{r}
#| label: data
turbidity <- c(Upper = 4.2, Middle = 7.9, Lower = 12.6)
n_high <- sum(turbidity > 10)
change <- -0.084
```

We sampled `r length(turbidity)`{.word} sites.
[No site | One site | # sites]{n="n_high"} read above the trigger.
Mean turbidity [rose by # | fell by #]{.pct sign="change"} on last year,
and the highest reading was `r claim(max(turbidity), . < 50)`{.num} NTU.
````

It renders as:

> We sampled three sites. One site read above the trigger. Mean
> turbidity fell by 8.4% on last year, and the highest reading was 12.6
> NTU.

If the data change so that no site reads above the trigger, the second
sentence becomes “No site read above the trigger.” If the highest
reading reaches 50, the render fails and names the line, instead of
printing a sentence that has stopped being true.

## Installation

weft is not on CRAN. Install the development version from GitHub:

``` r

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("vorpalvorpal/weft")
```

or

``` r

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("vorpalvorpal/weft")
```

weft uses the units package, which needs the udunits-2 library. The CRAN
binaries for macOS and Windows include it. On Linux, install your
distribution’s udunits-2 development package first (for example
`libudunits2-dev` on Debian and Ubuntu).

## The main ideas

**Values and formatters.** Inline R with an attribute block, such as
`` `r x`{.num} ``, prints a computed value through a formatter: a
number, a percentage, a spelled count, a list joined with “and”. Inline
R with no attribute block prints exactly as knitr prints it. See [Values
and
formatters](https://vorpalvorpal.github.io/weft/articles/values.html).

**Wording that depends on a value.** A span such as
`[a site | # sites]{n="k"}` chooses its words from a value: a plural
form, a direction, a condition being true. Each case you expect gets its
own wording. See [Value-dependent wording and
claims](https://vorpalvorpal.github.io/weft/articles/wording.html).

**Claims.** `claim(x, . > 10)` returns `x` unchanged and checks it. When
a check fails, the render fails with a report that names the sentence,
instead of printing a sentence the data no longer support. See
[Value-dependent wording and
claims](https://vorpalvorpal.github.io/weft/articles/wording.html).

**Units and the dictionary.** `u(35, m)` makes a number with a unit, and
weft prints the unit for you. The dictionary file `dict.yml` holds the
values a project chose, such as a threshold or a reporting year, each
with its definition. See [Units and the
dictionary](https://vorpalvorpal.github.io/weft/articles/units.html) and
[Using weft with
targets](https://vorpalvorpal.github.io/weft/articles/targets.html).

**Python and Julia chunks.** In an `.Rmd`, or a `.qmd` with
`engine: knitr`, a Python value reaches prose as
`` `r py$depth`{.num} `` and a Julia value as
`` `r jl_value("depth")`{.num} ``. weft reads each value itself and
refuses one that R cannot hold exactly. See [Python and Julia
chunks](https://vorpalvorpal.github.io/weft/articles/languages.html).

**Values by name.** A document that is not knit, such as a Quarto `.qmd`
on the Jupyter or Julia engine, has no R to evaluate prose. Write the
value as a name, `` `depth`{.num} ``, publish it from R
([`weft_put()`](https://vorpalvorpal.github.io/weft/reference/weft_put.md)),
Python (`put()`) or Julia (`@put`), and a Pandoc filter fills it in. The
same filter resolves conditions on names, wording, checks and values
files. See [Values by
name](https://vorpalvorpal.github.io/weft/articles/named-values.html).

**Lints.**
[`lints()`](https://vorpalvorpal.github.io/weft/reference/lints.md)
reads a project’s documents without running them and lists typed
numbers, construct errors and other problems. See [The static
lints](https://vorpalvorpal.github.io/weft/articles/lints.html).

**The commit gate and
[`verify()`](https://vorpalvorpal.github.io/weft/reference/verify.md).**
A git hook refuses a commit that adds a typed number or a construct
error, or that removes computed values without saying so.
[`verify()`](https://vorpalvorpal.github.io/weft/reference/verify.md)
renders the whole project and checks every claim before a release. See
[The commit gate, the ledger and
verify()](https://vorpalvorpal.github.io/weft/articles/gate.html).

**Setting up a project.**
[`use_weft()`](https://vorpalvorpal.github.io/weft/reference/use_weft.md)
writes everything a project needs, and says what it will write first.
See [Setting up a
project](https://vorpalvorpal.github.io/weft/articles/setup.html). If an
AI coding agent edits your documents, read [Working with coding
agents](https://vorpalvorpal.github.io/weft/articles/agents.html).

Start with [Getting
started](https://vorpalvorpal.github.io/weft/articles/weft.html).

## Status

weft is a development version (0.0.0.9001). It is not on CRAN, and its
functions and file formats may still change. The design is in
`dev/PACKAGE-SCOPING.md` in the repository. Please report problems at
<https://github.com/vorpalvorpal/weft/issues>.

## Values by name

Publish values under names, for prose that refers to them by name.

- [`weft_put()`](https://vorpalvorpal.github.io/weft/reference/weft_put.md)
  : Publish values by name
- [`weft_values_write()`](https://vorpalvorpal.github.io/weft/reference/weft_values_write.md)
  : Write a values file

## Wording that depends on values

- [`plural()`](https://vorpalvorpal.github.io/weft/reference/plural.md)
  : Choose a plural form

  Check a value in place

## Checking wording

See which arms a document can choose, and what the last knit did.

- [`arms()`](https://vorpalvorpal.github.io/weft/reference/arms.md) :
  List the arms of every governed span of a document
- [`rehearse()`](https://vorpalvorpal.github.io/weft/reference/rehearse.md)
  : Knit a document under several cases and see which arms they choose
- [`last_knit()`](https://vorpalvorpal.github.io/weft/reference/last_knit.md)
  : The records of the most recent knit
